name: commit-defender
description: AI-powered pre-commit code review that surfaces priority-graded findings inline in VS Code and blocks commits on critical issues.

commitDefender.pythonExecutable.description: Path to the Python executable that has commit-defender installed. Leave empty to auto-detect from the VS Code Python extension's selected interpreter, then fall back to 'python3'. You can also use ${workspaceFolder} as a prefix (e.g. ${workspaceFolder}/.venv/bin/python). Extension-only — no env var.

commitDefender.envFile.markdownDescription:
Path to a `.env` file containing `CD_*` environment variables (e.g. `~/.commit-defender.env`). Use this to keep credentials and provider settings out of VS Code settings and source control. VS Code settings take precedence over env file values when both are set. Extension-only — the path itself is not a `CD_*` variable.

Per-provider endpoints:

* `aoai`: `https://YOUR_RESOURCE.openai.azure.com`
* `anthropic`: `https://api.anthropic.com/v1`
* `openai`: `https://api.openai.com/v1`
* `gemini`: `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models`

enumDescriptions: aoai (Azure OpenAI): Azure-hosted OpenAI models. Requires endpoint, api-version, and a deployment name as the model.
anthropic: Anthropic Claude models (claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-opus-4-6, etc.).
openai: OpenAI platform (api.openai.com). Works with any model name like gpt-4o, o3, etc.
gemini: Google Gemini models (gemini-2.5-pro, gemini-2.5-flash, etc.). Requires GEMINI_API_KEY.
commitDefender.aiProvider.description: AI provider to use for code review. All providers return P0–P3 priority-graded comments. P3 Critical findings block the commit regardless of provider. Env var: CD_AI_PROVIDER.

commitDefender.model.description: Model or deployment name to use. Examples: 'claude-sonnet-4-6' (Anthropic), 'gpt-4o' (OpenAI), your deployment name (Azure). Env var: CD_MODEL.

commitDefender.endpoint.markdownDescription:
API endpoint URL. Required for `aoai`. For `openai`, `anthropic`, and `gemini`, leave empty to use the default public endpoint shown below.

Per-provider endpoints:

| Provider | Endpoint |
|---|---|
| `aoai` | `https://YOUR_RESOURCE.openai.azure.com` |
| `anthropic` | `https://api.anthropic.com/v1` |
| `openai` | `https://api.openai.com/v1` |
| `gemini` | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models` |

Env var: `CD_ENDPOINT`.

commitDefender.apiVersion.description: API version string. Used by aoai only (e.g. 2024-08-01-preview). Ignored for anthropic and openai. Env var: CD_API_VERSION.

commitDefender.apiKey.description: API key for the selected provider. Store this in User Settings (not Workspace) to keep it out of source control. Alternatively, set it in an Env File. Env var: CD_API_KEY.

commitDefender.maxTokens.description: Maximum output tokens for the AI review response. Increase if you see 'Could not parse AI response as JSON' on large diffs — the response was truncated before the JSON closed, which can cause P3 findings to be missed. Env var: CD_MAX_TOKENS.

enumDescriptions: hybrid: Run linters first, then send results + diff to AI for a combined review with P0–P3 priority grading.
ai-powered: Skip linters — send only the diff to the AI. Faster, no toolchain required. P0–P3 priority grading still applies.
rule-based: Run linters only — no AI call. Fully offline, deterministic. No priority grading (linter severity only).
commitDefender.analysisMode.description: Controls which analysis engines run. Hybrid and ai-powered modes produce P0–P3 priority-graded comments. P3 findings always block the commit. Env var: CD_ANALYSIS_MODE.

enumDescriptions: severe: Zero tolerance — nearly all findings become P2 (Warning) or P3 (Critical).
rigorous: Strict — style issues escalate to P2 (Warning), most things flagged.
moderate: Balanced — P1/P2/P3 assigned by genuine impact. (default)
generous: Lenient — minor things become P1 (Info); only real risks reach P2/P3.
lean: Minimal — only P3 Critical (security, syntax errors, data-loss) issues flagged.
commitDefender.severityLevel.description: Controls how strictly the AI assigns priority levels. P1=Info (optional), P2=Warning (recommended), P3=Critical (blocks commit). Env var: CD_SEVERITY_LEVEL.

enumDescriptions: colorful: Elaborate feedback with examples, alternatives, and detailed explanations.
chatty: Detailed feedback with helpful context for each finding.
moderate: Standard amount of detail — clear but concise. (default)
simple: Brief, to-the-point findings with minimal explanation.
silent: One-line summaries only — no elaboration.
commitDefender.richnessLevel.description: Controls the verbosity and detail level of each priority comment's explanation. Env var: CD_RICHNESS_LEVEL.

enumDescriptions: en: English
ko: 한국어
commitDefender.locale.description: Language for AI review output. Env var: CD_LOCALE.

commitDefender.excludePatterns.description: Additional gitignore-style patterns to exclude from analysis (e.g. 'tests/**', '*.generated.ts'). Env var: CD_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS (comma-separated, e.g. 'tests/**,*.generated.ts').

enumDescriptions: Theme Adaptive — inherits priority colors from your active VS Code theme via CSS variables. Recommended default.
Cobalt9 — electric navy-friendly accents tuned for Cobalt2/Cobalt9 themes.
Tailwind — modern web palette, high saturation, familiar.
Pastel Soft — low saturation, gentle on the eyes. Best on light themes.
Material — Google Material A-tones, punchy.
Solarized — muted terminal-familiar tones, lower contrast.
Muted Modern — Tailwind × Solarized blend; works on both light and dark themes.
Nord — arctic, cool, low visual noise.
Dracula — classic purple/pink/cyan dark-theme accents.
Gruvbox — 70s retro, earthy warm tones.
CVD Consensus (colorblind-safe) — balanced across light and dark themes.
CVD Deep (colorblind-safe) — darker tones tuned for light themes.
CVD Vivid (colorblind-safe) — electric tones tuned for dark themes.
Okabe-Ito (colorblind-safe) — canonical palette from Nature methodology papers.
commitDefender.colorPalette.markdownDescription:
Color palette for priority badges and category chips in the Commit Defender summary panel.

- **Default**: `theme-adaptive` inherits from your active VS Code theme.
- **Normal-vision**: `cobalt9`, `tailwind`, `pastel-soft`, `material`, `solarized`, `muted-modern`, `nord`, `dracula`, `gruvbox`.
- **Colorblind-safe**: `cvd-consensus`, `cvd-deep`, `cvd-vivid`, `okabe-ito`.

Changes re-render the open summary panel automatically. Extension-only — no env var.

commitDefender.runOnStage.description: Automatically analyze whenever files are staged (git add). Also available manually via the shield icon. Extension-only — no env var.

enumDescriptions: enable: Automatically install the git pre-commit hook in the workspace repository on activation. The hook runs commit-defender on every git commit.
disable: Do not install or manage the git pre-commit hook. Analysis is still available manually and on git stage.
commitDefender.preCommitHook.description: Controls whether the git pre-commit hook is automatically installed in the workspace repository. Extension-only — no env var.

commitDefender.fileTimeoutSeconds.description: Maximum seconds to wait when analyzing a single file. Set to 0 for no limit. Extension-only — no env var.

commitDefender.directoryTimeoutSeconds.description: Maximum seconds to wait when analyzing a directory or the full repository. Set to 0 for no limit. Extension-only — no env var.

commitDefender.stagedFilesWarnThreshold.description: Show a warning prompt when the number of staged files exceeds this threshold before running analysis. Set to 0 to disable the prompt. Env var: CD_STAGED_FILES_WARN_THRESHOLD.

commitDefender.repoAnalysisWarnThreshold.description: Show a confirmation prompt when analyzing the full repository and the file count exceeds this threshold. Set to 0 to disable the prompt. Env var: CD_REPO_ANALYSIS_WARN_THRESHOLD.
